links.outcome: LLM benchmark performance and rubric applicability when translated to the Japanese clinical context
links.effect: Modest performance drop in GPT-4.1 due to rubric mismatches; significant failure in the Japanese-native LLM-jp-3.1 for lacking clinical completeness; many rubric criteria need localisation.
links.quote: Our findings reveal a modest performance drop in GPT-4.1 due to rubric mismatches, as well as a significant failure in the Japanese-native model, which lacked the required clinical completeness.

unlisted_practices: Localising translated medical LLM benchmarks (e.g., a J-HealthBench) to national clinical guidelines, healthcare systems and cultural norms
Using an LLM-as-a-Judge to classify benchmark scenarios and rubric criteria for contextual gaps

screen.reason: This study evaluates LLM performance on a localized translation of HealthBench and examines the benchmark's clinical/cultural gaps for the Japanese context, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
